title: Consumer reports 0.6.1 did not fix docs/log.md clobbering
description: A lore consumer reports log.md still truncating on 0.6.1. NOT reproduced, and deliberately not closed as works-for-me. Evidence against, gathered 2026-09-13 against the PUBLISHED 0.6.1 binary (global install verified byte-identical to the registry tarball, shim removed): (1) worst-case unreachability -- a purpose-built fixture with a 15-entry log across 16 commits, history then replaced by an orphan commit carrying the identical tree so 100 percent of logged commits were unreachable; 15 of 15 carried forward plus the new commit, zero lost; (2) idempotency -- two further syncs byte-identical; (3) CRLF -- log.md rewritten with CRLF, zero lost, so the trailing-CR strip is live in the published bytes. opum-agent independently measured +1/-0 on its own repo and on a clean registry install. Remaining hypotheses, in order: the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 (different npm prefix, vendored node_modules/.bin/lore, or a session started before the update); a DIFFERENT failure mode being misattributed to LCLI-474; or a shape no fixture has covered. UNCLOSED PLATFORM GAP: only the darwin-arm64 binary was exercised. win32-x64 and win32-arm64 are separately compiled artifacts and CRLF is precisely where they diverge -- the CRLF test simulated CRLF bytes on macOS, which is not the same as the Windows binary on a core.autocrlf=true checkout. Ask the consumer's PLATFORM first; it is one question and it splits the search space.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The consumer platform is known, and if Windows the win32 binary is exercised on a core.autocrlf=true checkout rather than simulated CRLF on macOS
Which lore binary the consumer actually ran is established from their filesystem -- resolved path plus version -- not from npm view
Either a reproducing fixture exists and the defect is fixed, or the report is resolved as not-0.6.1 or as a distinct failure mode with that mode named
If a distinct failure mode, it gets its own task rather than being folded into LCLI-474s record

comments.body:
SESSION HANDOFF 2026-09-13 (session recycled for context budget, not a decision point). This task is the live investigation; the 0.6.1 release it came out of is DONE and needs nothing.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, all measured against the PUBLISHED 0.6.1 binary — global install verified as a real symlink to the npm artifact with the local dev shim removed, so this is not a local build:

  1. Worst-case unreachability. Purpose-built fixture: a 15-entry docs/log.md across 16 commits, history then replaced by an orphan commit carrying the identical tree, so 100% of logged commits were unreachable. This is the repo-recreation shape at full severity, not the two legacy entries the original LCLI-474 fixture used. RESULT: 15 of 15 carried forward plus the new commit = 16. Zero lost.
  2. Idempotency. Two further syncs on that tree: byte-identical output, still 16 entries.
  3. CRLF input. log.md rewritten with CRLF line endings, then synced. Zero lost — the trailing-CR strip is live in the published bytes.

opum-agent independently measured +1 line / -0 on its own repository and on a clean registry install of 0.6.1, and diffed the registry tarball's bin/lore.cjs against the global one (identical).

THE OPEN QUESTION IS THE CONSUMER'S PLATFORM, and it is the single highest-value thing to establish next. Everything above exercised the DARWIN-ARM64 binary only. @opum-ai/lore-win32-x64 and @opum-ai/lore-win32-arm64 are SEPARATELY COMPILED artifacts, and CRLF is precisely the axis on which they diverge — the CRLF test above simulated CRLF bytes on macOS, which is NOT the same as running the Windows binary against a core.autocrlf=true checkout. If the consumer is on Windows, this is untested territory and reproducing it needs a Windows runner. Ask the platform FIRST: it is one question and it splits the search space in half. Requesting a Windows runner is a decision for the user, not something to assume.

REMAINING HYPOTHESES, in the order worth testing: (1) the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 — a different npm prefix, a vendored node_modules/.bin/lore, or a session started before the update all show old behaviour while `npm view` says 0.6.1; (2) a DIFFERENT failure mode misattributed to LCLI-474 — entries vanishing because they reference commits unreachable after a squash merge or rebase is not the replace-vs-merge bug and 901646cf would not touch it; distinguish by asking WHICH lines survived (newest, oldest, or an arbitrary slice); (3) a shape no fixture has covered.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS AS WORKS-FOR-ME. Failing to reproduce is strictly weaker than knowing it does not happen. opum-agent said the same and was right to.

METHODOLOGICAL TRAP FOUND HERE, worth more than this bug. `git merge-base --is-ancestor abcabb4f v0.6.1` reported the LCLI-474 trailing-CR fix as ABSENT from 0.6.1. That is WRONG — the fix shipped; its branch was SQUASH-merged, so the original commit SHA is not an ancestor even though the change is in the tree. Verified by reading the bytes: `git show v0.6.1:src/core/log.ts` has the strip at line 277. This nearly became a reported root cause, because "CR fix missing" matched the reported symptom exactly. NEVER use --is-ancestor, --contains, or `git cherry` to decide whether a squash-merged change shipped. Read the bytes at the tag:
    git show <tag>:<path> | grep -n '<distinctive line>'

SKILLS THE SUCCESSOR SHOULD REACH FOR: opum-sdlc before branching or landing anything, opum-lore for any docs change (lore check exiting 0 is the definition of done), opum-quest for tracker writes.

STATE: branch chore/LCLI-484-log-report, PR #17 open, tracker-only. Nothing else in flight. LCLI-481, LCLI-482 and LCLI-483 are filed and untouched; LCLI-480 is parked at Blocked on its own branch with PR #12 open and is unrelated to any of tonight's work.

THIRD-PARTY NON-REPRODUCTION, 2026-09-13, from opum-cli-e2e. Logged as evidence, NOT as grounds to close.

opum-cli-e2e built its OWN repro rather than re-running this task's fixture -- orphaned/rewritten git history, matching the real recreation mechanism -- and ran it against the actual published 0.6.1 binary. All pre-existing docs/log.md entries survived the sync. They were explicit that this is a first-party result and not a restatement of ours.

That makes three independent non-reproductions on darwin-arm64: this task's 15-entry orphan fixture, opum-agent's +1/-0 measurement on its own repo and on a clean registry install, and now opum-cli-e2e's independent fixture. Their full matrix (427 rows) scores every lore-owned surface -- contract/lore, lore/lifecycle, lore/retrieval, lore/workspace, cross-product, packaging/lore -- at 100 percent pass, with tarball-digest corroboration against run 34783940117's six per-platform qualification reports. Their 8 fails and 2 blocked are all traced to their own harness's TASK-45 gap, to quest-cli's v0.6.0 tag no longer byte-matching its npm tarball, and to one routine out-of-band scale job. None is a lore defect.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the platform gap is still the open question and it is still the reason this stays open. Every one of the three non-reproductions exercised DARWIN-ARM64. win32-x64 and win32-arm64 are separately compiled artifacts and CRLF is exactly where they diverge. Three macOS non-reproductions are one non-reproduction with more witnesses; they do not add up to a Windows result. Ask the consumer's platform first -- that acceptance criterion is unchanged and unmet.

Recording the convergence because it does shift the priors on hypothesis (1) -- that the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 -- and because a future reader should not have to re-derive that three separate parties failed to reproduce this.

PLATFORM GAP NARROWED AT SOURCE LEVEL, 2026-09-13. This task's handoff said "CRLF is precisely the axis on which they diverge" about the win32 binaries. That framing is OVERSTATED, and the correction matters because it changes what to spend effort on next.

opum-cli-e2e ran a CRLF-plus-orphaned-history repro on the 0.6.1 darwin-arm64 binary -- 10 CRLF-terminated entries, all survived verbatim (comm -23 empty), 2 new entries derived correctly, output renormalised to LF. They were careful to state the limit themselves: not win32-native execution, so not proof about the compiled Windows artifact. Their added claim was that the CR handling lives in shared parsing logic rather than OS-specific I/O. VERIFIED HERE against the source rather than accepted:

  src/core/log.ts:277   const line = rawLine.endsWith("\r") ? rawLine.slice(0, -1) : rawLine;
  src/core/log.ts:276   for (const rawLine of existing.split("\n"))

parseEntries is pure string logic. grep for process.platform / os.EOL / win32 / EOL across src/core/log.ts returns NOTHING -- there is no platform branch in the file at all. And the bytes reach it untranslated: sync.ts:312 readFileIfPresent -> errors.ts:337 readFileSync(absPath, "utf8"), which performs no newline translation on any platform (neither Node nor Bun has a text mode). So what is on disk is what parseEntries sees, and a CRLF file written on macOS is byte-identical input to one a core.autocrlf=true checkout materialises on Windows.

CONSEQUENCE. The win32 binaries are compiled from this same platform-independent source, so for THIS code path there is no mechanism by which they could diverge. That does not make a Windows test worthless -- a compiled artifact differing from its source is exactly the kind of thing you cannot rule out by reading -- but it downgrades the platform hypothesis from "the most likely explanation" to "the one we have not physically executed". AC#1 is unchanged in value; AC#0 should no longer be treated as the FIRST thing to spend a Windows runner on.

REVISED HYPOTHESIS ORDER: (1) the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 -- different npm prefix, vendored node_modules/.bin/lore, or a session started before the update -- now clearly the leading explanation, with four non-reproductions behind it and the CRLF mechanism ruled out at source; (2) a DIFFERENT failure mode misattributed to LCLI-474, distinguished by asking WHICH lines survived (newest, oldest, or an arbitrary slice); (3) the win32 compiled artifact, kept alive but no longer leading.

STILL DO NOT CLOSE AS WORKS-FOR-ME. Four non-reproductions and a source-level argument are still not the consumer's machine. The next action is the same single question it has always been: which binary did they actually run, resolved path plus version, read off their filesystem rather than from npm view.

METHOD NOTE: the handoff's "CRLF is precisely where they diverge" was an inference from "these are separately compiled artifacts" plus "CRLF is a Windows thing". Neither premise was wrong; the conclusion did not follow, and ten minutes of reading the parser would have caught it before it shaped a whole session's priorities. Same shape as the npm/OIDC error on LCLI-482 the same night -- a mechanism asserted from plausible surroundings instead of checked in the code that actually does the work.

finalSummary:
RESOLVED: the report was real, the defect was not. The consumer's test asserted behaviour lore never promised, and 0.6.1's LCLI-474 fix passes their validation once the expectation is corrected. Closing on that, deliberately NOT as could-not-reproduce.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. The consumer's validation suite expected arbitrary AUTHORED PROSE placed in docs/log.md to survive a `lore sync`. It does not, and never has. Their test failed, and the failure was reported as 0.6.1 failing to fix the log.md clobbering defect. They found and corrected their own expectation and had the correction independently reviewed. Their suite now passes: full and scoped sync across complete and shallow git history, preserving dated entries, folder assignments, rendered subjects and repeated-sync byte stability -- 93 of 93 workflow tests including real Quest/Lore integration, on disposable repositories.

VERIFIED FIRST-PARTY, not accepted on the relay. src/core/log.ts documents parseEntries as total by construction: "A line that is neither a folder heading nor an entry -- prose, a stray hand edit, the `# Change log` title, a blank -- is skipped." Read the code: every non-matching line hits `continue`. So a regenerated log is a function of git history plus the entries still legible in the old file, and nothing else. That is exactly the behaviour the consumer's test contradicted, which independently corroborates the account of the resolution without relying on it.

WHY NOT could-not-reproduce. A task closed as unreproducible invites the next person to reopen it on the next report. This one has a named cause: the expectation was outside the documented contract. That tells a future reader what to check instead.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, honestly. AC#3 (distinct failure mode gets its own task) is met -- LCLI-485. AC#2 is met in its second branch: the report is resolved with the mode named. AC#0 (exercise the win32 binary on a core.autocrlf=true checkout) and AC#1 (establish which binary the consumer ran from their filesystem) are UNMET and now MOOT; they stay unchecked rather than being checked on faith. The Windows-runner question is withdrawn: it was a reasonable hypothesis and is now unnecessary. Stated explicitly so nobody provisions a runner later off a stale note.

THE WINDOWS HYPOTHESIS WAS ALREADY DEAD before this resolution arrived, on separate evidence: parseEntries is pure string logic, src/core/log.ts contains no platform branch at all, and the bytes reach it untranslated via readFileSync(path, "utf8"), which has no text mode on any platform. A CRLF file written on macOS is byte-identical input to one a core.autocrlf=true checkout materialises on Windows.

WHAT THIS COST, and what it bought. Four independent non-reproductions (this task's 15-entry orphan fixture, opum-agent's +1/-0 on two repos, opum-cli-e2e's independent fixture, and their CRLF variant), investigation across three repositories, and a serious proposal to provision a Windows CI runner -- all chasing a defect that did not exist. Nobody was wrong about the code. The disagreement was about what the generated log PROMISES, and the promise was written down only in a source comment. That gap is now LCLI-485, and this false alarm is its evidence.

THE METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING, because it was nearly load-bearing twice: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <tag>` reported the LCLI-474 trailing-CR fix ABSENT from 0.6.1. That is wrong -- the branch was squash-merged, so the original SHA is not an ancestor even though the change is in the tree. Never use --is-ancestor, --contains or `git cherry` to decide whether a squash-merged change shipped. Read the bytes at the tag: `git show <tag>:<path>`.

Consumer's detailed evidence: results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/ on the opum-cli-e2e host.
